summary: Part C0 of DiamondEtaleCohomology plans stages C0–C7, the étale cohomology of diamonds and small v-stacks of Scholze's 'Étale cohomology of diamonds' (ECD, arXiv:1709.07343v4) §§14 and 16–20, read in full. C0 constructs the étale site of a locally spatial diamond, the quasi-pro-étale site of a diamond and the v-site of a small v-stack with their cutoffs, the comparison morphisms λ_Y and ν_Y, the universal separated pro-étale quotient λ∘_X, enough points, continuity of étale cohomology, repleteness of the v- and quasi-pro-étale topoi by countable lifting towers, left-completeness and the bounded-below comparison (14.1–14.11). C1 proves Theorem 16.1 in its three separate cases and the base change corollaries for complexes with étale cohomology sheaves. C2 proves v-locality 14.12, defines D_ét(Y, Λ), identifies it with the left completion of D(Y_ét, Λ), and proves presentability at a cutoff, the étale coreflection and hyperdescent (17.1–17.4); Corollaries 16.5 and 16.8 sit here because they concern D_ét. C3 constructs f^∗, Rf∗, ⊗^L, RHom and change of coefficients with Proposition 17.6. C4 plans ECD §18 (proper and partially proper maps, valuative criteria, the canonical compactification and its universal property, tautness), resolving RT-AREA-padic-1/11 in favour of C4. C5 constructs extension by zero for étale maps and proves the proper base change theorem 19.2 through Lemma 19.4; C6 proves the three invariance statements of Theorem 19.5; C7 plans constructible sheaves and perfect-constructible complexes with their descent, limit and filtration theorems (20.1–20.8, 20.11–20.16), in the proof order the stage text fixes. Neither pinned library has perfectoid spaces, diamonds or their sites, so every target is a node; the generic carriers (Grothendieck topologies, sheaves, points of sites, derived categories, constructible sets, spectral spaces, finitely presentable objects) are cited from Mathlib, the diamond geometry from DiamondsAndVStacks, the enhanced sheaf theory from EnhancedDerivedSheaves, the classical inputs from ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology and perfect complexes from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7. Two source gaps (ECD 14.7 in degrees ≥ 2 and the vanishing step of 19.5(ii)) are recorded as gaps; nine supplier contracts are requested.

nodes.title: The étale site of a locally spatial diamond
nodes.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack on Perf that is a locally spatial diamond. The étale site Y_ét is the site whose objects are the étale maps Y′ → Y that are locally separated (Convention 10.2), whose morphisms are maps over Y, and whose coverings are the families {Y′_i → Y′} that are jointly surjective as maps of v-stacks on Perf. Every object Y′ is again a locally spatial diamond, and the topos Y_ét^∼ is the category of étale sheaves on Y.
proofSteps: Fibre products of étale maps are étale, and a map between two étale Y-objects is étale (two-out-of-three for étale maps, DiamondsAndVStacks D5), so Y_ét has all finite limits, computed in small v-stacks; equalizers exist as well.
Isomorphisms cover, coverings are stable under base change because surjectivity of maps of v-stacks is (D4), and composites of coverings cover; so the jointly surjective families form a pretopology.
An étale map into a locally spatial diamond has locally spatial source (D5 permanence for étale and quasi-pro-étale maps into locally spatial diamonds), so Y_ét consists of locally spatial diamonds.

Étale maps are open on underlying spaces, so a family of étale maps is jointly surjective as v-stacks exactly when the images of the |Y′_i| cover |Y′| (the argument at the end of the proof of ECD Proposition 14.3).
The quasicompact separated étale maps form a basis (node etale-to-quasi-pro-etale-basis), and they form an essentially small category, so Y_ét^∼ is a Grothendieck topos without any cutoff.
acceptance: For a perfectoid space X the site X_ét agrees with the étale site of the perfectoid space X, and for an analytic adic space Z over Z_p the site (Z^♢)_ét agrees with Z_ét (ECD Lemma 15.6).

nodes.title: The quasi-pro-étale site of a diamond
nodes.statement: Let Y be a diamond. The quasi-pro-étale site Y_qproét is the site whose objects are the quasi-pro-étale maps Y′ → Y that are locally separated (Convention 10.2), whose morphisms are maps over Y, and whose coverings are the families that are jointly surjective as maps of v-stacks on Perf. For every cutoff cardinal κ (ECD Lemma 4.1) Y_qproét,κ is the full subsite of κ-small objects; small sheaves on Y_qproét form the large filtered colimit of the topoi Y_qproét,κ^∼ along the fully faithful restriction functors.
proofSteps: Every source Y′ of a quasi-pro-étale map to Y is a small v-sheaf (D3, D5), fibre products of quasi-pro-étale maps are quasi-pro-étale and maps between quasi-pro-étale Y-objects are quasi-pro-étale (two-out-of-three, D5), so finite limits exist.
Jointly surjective families form a pretopology by the same argument as for Y_ét.

For cutoff cardinals κ ≤ κ′ the inclusion Y_qproét,κ ⊂ Y_qproét,κ′ induces fully faithful functors on sheaf topoi which preserve cohomology (DiamondsAndVStacks D2, cutoff independence, ECD §8.2), and small sheaves are those defined at some κ.
acceptance: For a strictly totally disconnected X, small sheaves on X_qproét are the sheaves on the coherent site of quasicompact separated pro-étale maps (node perfectoid-bases-and-coherent-subsites).

nodes.title: The v-site of a small v-stack
nodes.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack on Perf. The v-site Y_v is the site whose objects are all maps Y′ → Y from small v-sheaves Y′, whose morphisms are maps over Y, and whose coverings are the jointly surjective families (as maps of v-stacks on Perf); for perfectoid spaces X and {X_i → X} this means a v-cover. For every cutoff cardinal κ there is the subsite Y_v,κ of κ-small objects, and small sheaves on Y_v form the large filtered colimit of the topoi Y_v,κ^∼.
proofSteps: Fibre products of small v-sheaves over the small v-stack Y are small v-sheaves (DiamondsAndVStacks D4), so Y_v has finite limits.
Jointly surjective families form a pretopology; for perfectoid spaces it is the v-topology of D2.
Cutoff independence and fully faithful transition functors as for Y_qproét (D2).

nodes.statement: Fix a ring Λ. For a topos T, D(T, Λ) is the derived category of sheaves of Λ-modules and D⁺, D⁻, D^b ⊂ D(T, Λ) are the cohomologically bounded below, above and bounded subcategories. For a diamond Y, resp. small v-stack Y, D(Y_qproét, Λ), resp. D(Y_v, Λ), is the filtered colimit over cutoff cardinals κ of D(Y_qproét,κ, Λ), resp. D(Y_v,κ, Λ), along fully faithful transition functors; the canonical t-structures and truncations are compatible with the transitions.
proofSteps: For κ ≤ κ′ the restriction of sheaves has an exact fully faithful left adjoint on module sheaves (extension from the smaller site), which preserves injective-acyclicity of the relevant objects by cutoff independence of cohomology (D2); hence the derived functor D(Y_v,κ, Λ) → D(Y_v,κ′, Λ) is fully faithful and t-exact.
Take the filtered colimit of categories; truncations, shifts and cones are computed at any cutoff containing the data.

nodes.title: The étale, quasi-pro-étale and v-topoi are algebraic
nodes.statement: The categories of small sheaves on Y_ét, Y_qproét and Y_v, for Y a locally spatial diamond, a diamond and a small v-stack respectively, are algebraic topoi (at each cutoff for the last two). If Y is 0-truncated (a small v-sheaf), an object of any of these sites is quasicompact, resp. quasiseparated, in the topos-theoretic sense if and only if it is quasicompact, resp. quasiseparated, as a small v-stack on Perf.
proofSteps: ECD leaves the proof to the reader. Generating families: the quasicompact separated étale maps for Y_ét (Corollary 11.28), and the affinoid, or strictly totally disconnected, perfectoid spaces over Y (κ-small) for the other two sites.

These generators are quasicompact objects, fibre products of two of them over a quasiseparated object are quasicompact, and they are stable under fibre products in the qcqs subsites; this is the criterion for an algebraic topos (D0's coherent-topos interface, SGA 4 VI 2.3), as in D2 for the perfectoid sites.

For 0-truncated Y, compare the topos notions with quasicompactness of small v-sheaves through the covering characterization: an object is quasicompact iff every covering family has a finite subcover, which for small v-sheaves is ECD's quasicompactness.
acceptance: The proof is written out here because the source omits it; the generating families named in the first step are the ones the proofs of ECD 14.4 and 14.8 use.

nodes.title: Stalks of étale sheaves at geometric points
nodes.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond and y ∈ |Y|. Choose a quasi-pro-étale map ȳ : Spa(C(y), C(y)⁺) → Y with C(y) algebraically closed, C(y)⁺ ⊂ C(y) an open and bounded valuation subring, mapping the closed point to y. For a sheaf F on Y_ét put F_ȳ = colim_{ȳ → U ∈ Y_ét} F(U). The index category is cofiltered over U, and F ↦ F_ȳ is pullback along ȳ_ét followed by global sections on Spa(C(y), C(y)⁺)_ét; it is a point of the topos Y_ét^∼.
proofSteps: Equalizers exist in Y_ét, so the colimit is filtered.
Identify F_ȳ with Γ(Spa(C(y), C(y)⁺), ȳ_ét^∗F): ȳ is a cofiltered limit of étale neighbourhoods in the sense of D5's finite-stage comparison.

Let F_0 be an étale sheaf on Y_0 with pullbacks F_i to Y_i and F to Y. Then colim_i H^j(Y_i, F_i) → H^j(Y, F) is an isomorphism for j = 0 if F_0 is a sheaf of sets, for j = 0, 1 if it is a sheaf of groups, and for all j ≥ 0 if it is a sheaf of abelian groups. Relative form: for i_0 ∈ I and f_i : Y → Y_i, f_{i,i_0} : Y_i → Y_{i_0}, one has R^q f_{i_0∗}F = colim_{i→i_0} R^q f_{i,i_0∗}F_i on (Y_{i_0})_ét.
proofSteps: Transition maps between spatial diamonds are qcqs, and Y is a spatial diamond (D5).

Replace each étale site by its quasicompact separated part. By ECD Proposition 11.23(iii) (D5), the quasicompact separated étale objects over Y form the 2-colimit of those over the Y_i; finite jointly surjective families descend to a finite stage because |Y| = lim |Y_i| and quasicompact opens of a cofiltered limit of spectral spaces come from a finite stage (PerfectoidSpaces P5). So Y_ét,qc,sep^∼ is the limit of the fibred coherent topos (Y_i)_ét,qc,sep^∼.

Apply the theorem on cohomology of a cofiltered limit of coherent topoi with coherent transition maps (SGA 4 VI 8.7.7), requested from DiamondsAndVStacks D0, the owner of the ordinary topos interfaces. The relative form follows by applying the absolute form to the systems Y_i ×_{Y_{i_0}} U for quasicompact separated étale U → Y_{i_0}.
acceptance: Concrete instance (ECD proof of 19.5(ii)): H^i of a perfectoid annulus is the colimit of H^i of the annuli Y′_{n,L} over finite extensions L of k((t^{1/p^∞})).

nodes.title: The étale topos of a strictly totally disconnected space
nodes.statement: Let X be a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space. Then X_ét^∼ is equivalent to the topos of sheaves on |X|, every étale cover of a quasicompact open U ⊂ X splits, and H^i(U_ét, F) = 0 for all i > 0, all sheaves of abelian groups F and all quasicompact open U; in particular these U form a basis of X_ét of objects with vanishing higher cohomology.
proofSteps: Quasicompact opens U of a strictly totally disconnected space are strictly totally disconnected (pro-constructible generalizing subsets, D1 api) and every étale cover of such U splits (D1, definition). For an étale V → X and a quasicompact open U in its image, V ×_X U → U splits, and a section of a locally separated étale map is an open immersion; so every étale map to X is locally on the source an open immersion, and V ↦ |V| gives X_ét^∼ ≃ Sh(|X|), also for Λ-modules and compatibly with pullback.
If every cover of U splits, a sheaf surjection is surjective on U-sections, so Γ(U, −) is exact and H^i(U, F) = 0 for i > 0.

nodes.title: The quasi-pro-étale topos of a diamond is replete
nodes.statement: Let Y be a diamond and κ a cutoff cardinal. The topos Y_qproét,κ^∼ (hence the category of small sheaves on Y_qproét) is replete: for every sequence of epimorphisms of sheaves ⋯ → F_2 → F_1 → F_0, the map lim_n F_n → F_0 is an epimorphism.
proofSteps: Strictly totally disconnected spaces quasi-pro-étale over Y form a basis (node perfectoid-bases-and-coherent-subsites), and every covering of such X in Y_qproét is refined by a single affinoid pro-étale surjection X_1 → X with X_1 strictly totally disconnected (D1: universally open strictly totally disconnected covers; quasicompact separated pro-étale maps over X are affinoid pro-étale).

Countable lifting tower: lift s_0 ∈ F_0(X) along affinoid pro-étale surjections X_{n+1} → X_n with lifts s_{n+1} ∈ F_{n+1}(X_{n+1}); X_∞ = lim X_n is affinoid pro-étale over X (cofiltered limits of affinoid pro-étale maps, PerfectoidSpaces P6), κ-small for an adequate κ, and X_∞ → X is surjective (inverse limit of surjective spectral maps), hence a covering in Y_qproét.

The sections s_n|X_∞ give a section of lim F_n lifting s_0. ECD instead uses the basis of strictly w-local spaces with extremally disconnected π0, on which every pro-étale cover splits; the tower argument avoids that input and is the one the stage text asks for.

nodes.title: The v-topos of a small v-stack is replete
nodes.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack and κ a cutoff cardinal. The topos Y_v,κ^∼ (and hence the category of small sheaves on Y_v) is replete: for every sequence of epimorphisms of sheaves ⋯ → F_2 → F_1 → F_0, the map lim_n F_n → F_0 is an epimorphism.
proofSteps: Countable lifting tower: given s_0 ∈ F_0(X) with X affinoid perfectoid over Y, choose inductively affinoid perfectoid v-covers X_{n+1} → X_n and lifts s_{n+1} ∈ F_{n+1}(X_{n+1}) of s_n|X_{n+1}, using that every v-cover of an affinoid perfectoid space is refined by one affinoid perfectoid space.

X_∞ = lim_n X_n is affinoid perfectoid (cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces, PerfectoidSpaces P5), κ-small for a cutoff κ (P6), and X_∞ → X is a v-cover because an inverse limit of surjective spectral maps of spectral spaces is surjective.
The compatible sections s_n|X_∞ give a section of lim F_n over X_∞ lifting s_0, so lim F_n → F_0 is an epimorphism.
This is the input [BS15, Proposition 3.3.3] needs; ECD asserts repleteness without proof.
acceptance: The tower is countable; no choice beyond countable dependent choice of covers is used, and the cutoff κ is fixed in advance so that X_∞ stays κ-small.

nodes.title: The enhanced v-derived categories at a cutoff and their functoriality
nodes.statement: For a small v-stack Y, a ring Λ and a cutoff cardinal κ, the ∞-derived category 𝒟(Y_v,κ, Λ) of sheaves of Λ-modules on Y_v,κ is a presentable stable ∞-category with homotopy category D(Y_v,κ, Λ); the transition functors for κ ≤ κ′ and the pullbacks f_v^∗ along 0-truncated maps are colimit-preserving exact functors of ∞-categories, with coherent compatibility data under change of cutoff and composition. For a simplicial small v-stack Y_• with 0-truncated face maps, 𝒟(Y_•,v, Λ) is the ∞-derived category of the simplicial site, with its full subcategory 𝒟_cart(Y_•,v, Λ) of cartesian objects.

Cutoff transitions are fully faithful on homotopy categories (C0), hence fully faithful as functors of ∞-categories.
The simplicial site of Y_• is a diagram of ringed topoi; its ∞-derived category and cartesian subcategory come from E3.

nodes.title: Pullback f^∗ on D(Y_v, Λ) and D_ét for arbitrary maps of small v-stacks
nodes.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of small v-stacks. Choose a perfectoid space Y′_0 with a surjection Y′_0 → Y′ and let Y′_• be its Čech nerve; all Y′_i are small v-sheaves and Y′_i → Y′, Y′_i → Y are 0-truncated. Pullback along Y′_• → Y gives f_v^∗ : 𝒟(Y_v, Λ) → 𝒟_cart(Y′_•,v, Λ) ≃ 𝒟(Y′_v, Λ), which carries 𝒟_ét(Y, Λ) into 𝒟_ét(Y′, Λ) and restricts to f^∗ : D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Y′, Λ). The functor is canonically independent of the choice of Y′_0 → Y′ and, for g : Y″ → Y′, there is a natural equivalence (f ∘ g)^∗ ≃ g^∗ ∘ f^∗ with the usual coherences. For 0-truncated f it is the pullback of the morphism of sites f_v.
proofSteps: For 0-truncated f, f_v is a morphism of sites and f_v^∗ is the pullback of ringed topoi (C2/enhanced-v-derived-category).
In general, pull back to the Čech nerve, which consists of 0-truncated maps, and use hyperdescent (C2/v-hyperdescent) to identify cartesian objects on Y′_• with 𝒟(Y′_v, Λ).

Independence: the choices of Y′_0 → Y′ form a cofiltered category, and refinements induce equivalences compatible with the identifications. Composition: composites of pullbacks are pullbacks on Čech nerves. The printed law (f ∘ g)^∗ ≃ f^∗ ∘ g^∗ is a misprint for g^∗ ∘ f^∗ (PAPER-SCHOLZE-17/E92), and 𝒟_ét(Y_v, Λ) is a misprint for 𝒟_ét(Y, Λ) (PAPER-SCHOLZE-17/E93).

Preservation of D_ét: test on strictly totally disconnected X → Y′; the composite X → Y is a map from a strictly totally disconnected space. The referee's alternative: the cocontinuous functor Y′_v → Y_v, (X′ → Y′) ↦ (X′ → Y′ → Y), gives the same pullback.

nodes.title: Proper maps of v-stacks
nodes.statement: A map f : Y′ → Y of v-stacks is proper if it is quasicompact, separated and universally closed: for every small v-sheaf X with a map X → Y, the map |Y′ ×_Y X| → |X| is closed. Since f is quasicompact, Y′ ×_Y X is a small v-sheaf for small X, and it suffices to test universal closedness on perfectoid X, or even on strictly totally disconnected perfectoid X.
proofSteps: Quasicompact, separated and the underlying space |−| of a small v-sheaf are DiamondsAndVStacks notions (D3, D4).

The reduction of the test to strictly totally disconnected X uses that |X| carries the quotient topology from any v-cover by perfectoid spaces (D4) and that such covers can be refined by strictly totally disconnected ones (D1).
acceptance: Universal closedness, separatedness, properness and partial properness are four distinct predicates; none is replaced by another.

nodes.title: Properness for maps of locally compact Hausdorff spaces
nodes.statement: Let T′ → T be a continuous map of locally compact Hausdorff spaces and T̲′ → T̲ the induced map of v-sheaves (X ↦ C(|X|, T)). Then T̲′ → T̲ is proper in the sense of Definition 18.1 if and only if T′ → T is proper in the usual sense (preimages of compact subsets are compact; equivalently universally closed).
proofSteps: T̲ is the filtered colimit of the compact Hausdorff v-sheaves K̲ over compact K ⊂ T along closed immersions, and |T̲| = T (DiamondsAndVStacks D4, compact Hausdorff spaces as diamonds); a map from a quasicompact |X| to T lands in some K.
Separatedness: T′ is Hausdorff, so the diagonal of T̲′ → T̲ is the v-sheaf of a closed subset of T′ ×_T T′, a closed immersion.
Quasicompactness: T̲′ ×_T̲ K̲ = (f^{−1}K)̲, which is quasicompact iff f^{−1}K is compact; so f quasicompact ⇔ preimages of compacta are compact.

Universal closedness: for perfectoid X → T̲, |T̲′ ×_T̲ X| = T′ ×_T |X| and the projection is closed when T′ → T is proper (proper maps of topological spaces are universally closed). Conversely proper ⇒ quasicompact ⇒ topologically proper.
The source leaves this to the reader (PAPER-SCHOLZE-17/411); the steps above supply it.
acceptance: Concrete instance: for a profinite set S, S̲ → ∗ is proper, while Z̲ → ∗ (Z discrete, infinite) is partially proper but not proper.

nodes.title: Valuative criterion of properness
nodes.statement: A map f : Y′ → Y of v-stacks is proper if and only if it is 0-truncated, quasicompact and quasiseparated, and for every perfectoid field K with an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K and every commutative square Spa(K, O_K) → Y′, Spa(K, K⁺) → Y there is a unique lift Spa(K, K⁺) → Y′. Moreover, if f is proper, then for every perfectoid Tate ring R with an open and integrally closed subring R⁺ ⊂ R, every square Spa(R, R°) → Y′, Spa(R, R⁺) → Y has a unique lift Spa(R, R⁺) → Y′.
proofSteps: ⇐: separatedness from the valuative criterion of separatedness (ECD Proposition 10.9, D3). For closedness reduce to Y = X affinoid perfectoid and Y′ qcqs with an affinoid perfectoid cover X′ → Y′. The image W ⊂ |X| of a closed Z ⊂ |Y′| is pro-constructible (image under the spectral map |X′| → |X|); it is closed once specializing, and a specialization w ⇝ w′ with w ∈ W is realized by Spa(K, K⁺) → Spa(K, (K⁺)′) → X; the unique lift and density of Spa(K, K⁺) in Spa(K, (K⁺)′) put w′ in W.

⇒ (the (R, R⁺) form, which contains the (K, K⁺) form): uniqueness by ECD Proposition 10.10 (D3). For existence replace Y by Spa(R, R⁺); Spa(R, R°) → Y′ is a quasicompact injection determined by its image (ECD 12.15, D4). Its closure Z in |Y′| pulls back to the closure of a pro-constructible generalizing subset of a totally disconnected cover (ECD Corollary 10.6, D3), so Z is a qcqs sub-v-sheaf; Z → Spa(R, R⁺) is injective (separated, and bijective on rank-one points) and surjective because |f| is universally closed and |Spa(R, R°)| is dense; hence an isomorphism by ECD Lemma 2.5 (D0) and 12.15, giving the lift.

nodes.title: The envelope is partially proper, and envelopes of quasicompact maps are proper
nodes.statement: Let Y be a separated v-sheaf. Then Ȳ is partially proper, and if f : Y′ → Y is a quasicompact map of separated v-sheaves, then f̄ : Ȳ′ → Ȳ is proper.
proofSteps: Quasiseparatedness of Ȳ → ∗: with Z = Spa(F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))) (so Z̄ = Z) and affinoid perfectoid X_1, X_2 → Ȳ × Z, write X_1 ×_{Ȳ×Z} X_2 = X_1 ×_{X̄_1} (X̄_1 ×_{Ȳ×Z} X̄_2) ×_{X̄_2} X_2 using limits (node compactification-limits-surjectivity), with X_i → X̄_i quasicompact by the affinoid formula and X̄_1 ×_{Ȳ×Z} X̄_2 quasicompact by surjectivity and quasiseparatedness of Y.
The lifting property holds by construction on totally disconnected Spa(R, R⁺), hence in general by v-descent; 0-truncatedness is clear.

For quasicompact f, f̄ is partially proper (source partially proper, target separated) and quasicompact by the affinoid formula, limits and surjectivity, so proper (node proper-iff-partially-proper-qc).

nodes.title: The canonical compactification of a separated map of v-stacks
nodes.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of v-stacks. The functor on totally disconnected perfectoid spaces X = Spa(R, R⁺) over Y, X ↦ Y′(R, R°) ×_{Y(R,R°)} Y(R, R⁺), extends to a v-stack Ȳ′^{/Y} with a map f̄^{/Y} : Ȳ′^{/Y} → Y and a natural map Y′ → Ȳ′^{/Y} over Y. Its formation is functorial in f and commutes with base change in Y; for separated Y, Ȳ′^{/Y} = Ȳ′ ×_Ȳ Y.
proofSteps: If Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) is a v-cover of totally disconnected spaces, so is Spa(S, S°) → Spa(R, R°) (ECD Lemma 7.6, D1).

Work locally on Y (Y representable), so Ȳ′^{/Y} is a presheaf of sets; injectivity of restriction along the cover follows from the v-cover of rank-one loci, and descent of a compatible section reduces, by separatedness of Y′ → Y and ECD Proposition 10.10 (D3), to agreement on Spa(T, T°) and Spa(T, (T⁺)′).
Functoriality and base change are clear from the formula; the formula Ȳ′ ×_Ȳ Y for separated Y compares values on totally disconnected test objects.

nodes.title: Properties of the relative canonical compactification
nodes.statement: Let Y′ → Y be a separated map of v-stacks. (i) Ȳ′^{/Y} → Y is partially proper. (ii) If Y and Y′ are small v-stacks, Ȳ′^{/Y} is a small v-stack. (v) If f : Y′_2 → Y′_1 is a surjective map of separated v-stacks over Y, then f̄^{/Y} is surjective. (vi) If f is quasicompact, f̄^{/Y} is proper. (vii) If f is quasi-pro-étale, f̄^{/Y} is quasi-pro-étale.

nodes.title: Images of proper maps in separated targets
nodes.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of v-sheaves. If Z → Y is a proper map of v-sheaves and Z → Y′ is a map over Y, then the sheaf-theoretic image Z′ of Z in Y′ is proper over Y and closed in Y′.
proofSteps: Z′ is separated as a subsheaf of Y′ and quasicompact as a quotient of Z; the valuative criterion for Z′ follows from that of Z.
Closedness: Z′ is the image of the graph of Z → Y′, a closed subset of Z ×_Y Y′, under the projection to Y′, which is closed by properness of Z → Y.

nodes.title: Partially proper maps of v-sheaves are filtered colimits of proper ones
nodes.statement: A map f : Y′ → Y of v-sheaves is partially proper if and only if f is a (possibly large) filtered colimit of proper maps f_i : Y′_i → Y along closed immersions Y′_i → Y′_j. If Y′ is small, the colimit can be taken small.

⇒: consider all closed sub-v-sheaves of Y′ proper over Y. By node proper-image-closed the image of Y′_1 ⊔ Y′_2 is another one, so the category is filtered; for affinoid perfectoid Z → Y′, Z̄^{/Y} is proper over Y (node relative-compactification-properties(vi)) and Z → Y′ factors through the image of Z̄^{/Y} → Y′, a closed sub-v-sheaf proper over Y, so Y′ is the colimit.

nodes.title: Partial properness through tautness for locally spatial sources
nodes.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map from a locally spatial v-sheaf Y′ to a spatial v-sheaf Y. Then f is partially proper if and only if |Y′| is taut (quasiseparated, with quasicompact closures of quasicompact opens) and for every perfectoid field K with open bounded valuation subring K⁺ and every square Spa(K, O_K) → Y′, Spa(K, K⁺) → Y there is a unique lift Spa(K, K⁺) → Y′.

nodes.statement: Let Λ be noetherian, X a spectral space and F a sheaf of Λ-modules on X. nodes.title: Characterizations of constructible sheaves on spatial diamonds
nodes.statement: Let Λ be noetherian, Y a spatial diamond and F an étale sheaf of Λ-modules on Y. The following are equivalent: (i) F is constructible; (ii) F is compact in the category of étale sheaves of Λ-modules on Y; (iii) there is a stratification of |Y| into constructible locally closed subsets S_i such that for every strictly totally disconnected f : X → Y, f^∗F|_{f^{−1}(S_i)} is constant with finitely generated value. proofSteps: (iii) ⇒ (i) by definition; (i) ⇒ (ii) since compactness descends along a strictly totally disconnected cover (as in 20.5).

(ii) ⇒ (iii): call sheaves as in (iii) strongly constructible; they are closed under kernels, cokernels, images and extensions. By ECD Lemma 11.31 (D5) every étale sheaf is a quotient of sums of j_!Λ with j : U ↪ V → W ↪ Y (quasicompact open, finite étale, quasicompact open), so it suffices that such j_!Λ is strongly constructible; then compact sheaves are summands of strongly constructible ones.

nodes.statement: Let Λ be noetherian and Y a spatial diamond. An étale sheaf F of Λ-modules on Y is constructible if and only if F has a finite filtration whose graded pieces are of the form j_!(L|_Z), where j : U → Y is a quasicompact separated étale map, Z ⊂ |U| a constructible closed subset, and L a local system of finitely generated Λ-modules on U.

nodes.title: Perfect-constructible complexes form a thick subcategory
nodes.statement: For any ring Λ and small v-stack Y, D_ét,pc(Y, Λ) ⊂ D_ét(Y, Λ) is a thick triangulated subcategory: it contains 0, is closed under shifts, cones and direct summands.
proofSteps: Reduce to strictly totally disconnected X. Shifts are clear; for a cone of a map A → B choose a common refinement of the stratifications on which both are constant perfect; on a stratum S the map is locally constant (Hom of constant complexes on a totally disconnected stratum is locally constant, as in the proof of 20.12), so after a finite clopen refinement the cone is constant perfect. Summands: a summand of a constant perfect complex on S is locally constant with perfect value (a retract of a perfect complex is perfect), and constant after refinement.
The source says 'It is clear'; the steps above are the verification.

nodes.title: Perfect-constructibility through cohomology sheaves and stalks
nodes.statement: Let Λ be noetherian, Y a small v-stack and A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ). A is perfect-constructible if and only if A is locally bounded, each cohomology sheaf H^i(A) is constructible, and all geometric stalks of A are perfect complexes of Λ-modules.
proofSteps: ⇒ is clear on a strictly totally disconnected cover. ⇐: reduce to X strictly totally disconnected and then, by stratifying, to a totally disconnected spectral space S (each connected component has a unique closed point) and bounded B with constant finitely generated cohomology sheaves; show B is locally constant by induction on the length, using τ^{<b}B → B → H^b(B)[−b].

Key identity: RHom_{D(S,Λ)}(M, C) = Cont(S, RHom_Λ(M, C)) for finitely generated M and bounded C, by a finite free resolution of M and H^i(S, C) = Cont(S, H^i(C)); so the extension class is locally constant, and perfect stalks give perfect values.
acceptance: Concrete instance: for Λ = Z/ℓ² and Y = Spa(C, O_C), the constant complex Z/ℓ is bounded with constructible cohomology and perfect stalk only if Z/ℓ is a perfect Z/ℓ²-complex, which it is not; so it is not perfect-constructible.

restructure.proposal: At assembly, retire C8/strictly-disconnected-acyclic in favour of C0/std-etale-acyclic and point its consumers (C8/qpetale-direct-image) at the C0 node; one owner, no change of mathematics.

restructure.detail: C1's text asks for Theorem 16.1 'and its corollaries' while forbidding the use of the étale subcategory D_ét defined after 14.12. Corollaries 16.5 and 16.8 are statements about membership in D_ét of small v-stacks, so they are planned in C2 (nodes qproet-pushforward-etale, qcqs-pushforward-preserves-etale) right after Definition 14.13; Corollaries 16.4 and 16.9 are planned in C1 for complexes on the quasi-pro-étale site with étale cohomology sheaves, which C2 identifies with D_ét.
restructure.proposal: Add one sentence to C1 and C2: 'Corollaries 16.5 and 16.8, which concern D_ét of small v-stacks, are proved in C2 after Definition 14.13; C1 states 16.4 and 16.9 for complexes whose cohomology sheaves come from the étale site.'

restructure.detail: PrismaticCohomology--PR.8 requests from C0 the completed structure sheaves Ô_Y, Ô⁺_Y on Y_qproét (Mann–Werner) and quasi-pro-étale descent with Z_p coefficients. A diamond has no structure sheaf; Ô_Y exists only after choosing an untilt (Y over Spd Z_p with Y^♯), which is not in ECD §14 or in C0's text.
restructure.proposal: Route the completed structure sheaves of untilted diamonds to the layer that owns untilts and relative period sheaves (for example a DiamondsAndVStacks D6 continuation or the PrismaticCohomology layer itself); C0 supplies the site Y_qproét, its repleteness and the comparisons of this packet.
